userStories.title: Phase 9 — SQLite concurrency hardening
userStories.description: Per prd.md Phase 9 line 1718 'harden SQLite concurrency'. (a) Audit all sql.Open / auradb.Open call sites for PRAGMA setup. Current state: most callers set busy_timeout but coverage isn't uniform. (b) Centralize the PRAGMA bundle in internal/db.Open so every caller automatically gets: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, PRAGMA busy_timeout=10000 (was 5000 — bumped for cron + agent concurrency), PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY. (c) Add a WAL checkpoint cron (PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) every 6h) so the WAL file doesn't grow unbounded — wire via existing internal/cron.Scheduler. (d) Document SQLITE_BUSY handling: any handler that catches it should retry-with-jitter up to N times before failing the request — add a helper internal/db.RetryOnBusy(ctx, fn) wrapping the canonical pattern. (e) Tests: concurrent write benchmark that exceeds the old busy_timeout, asserts the new value handles it.

userStories.title: Phase 9 — docs: clarify memory vs storage
userStories.description: Per prd.md Phase 9 line 1714 'clarify memory versus storage'. The terms are used inconsistently across the codebase. (a) Create docs/MEMORY-VS-STORAGE.md explaining: 'memory' = what the agent reads back at retrieval time (compact_memory_documents, freshness-tracked, kind-typed). 'storage' = durable artifacts on disk (wiki/*.md files, source raw bytes, garage blobs). Memory is REBUILDABLE; storage is NOT. (b) For each internal/ subdirectory, classify which layer it belongs to (a table at the top of the doc). (c) Cross-reference the §5.7 prd.md section. (d) Add a 'cardinal rule' section: anyone adding a new long-term data store should declare 'storage or memory?' and follow the implications (storage needs backup/migration; memory needs a rebuild path).
